```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 13, fig.height = 8)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(furrr)
library(digest)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
source(here::here("scripts/Network.R"))
dir.create(here::here("reports/Results_files/figure-gfm"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(here::here("data"), showWarnings = FALSE)

N_WORKERS <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1)

run_cached <- function(cache_name, fn, hash_obj) {
  hash       <- digest::digest(hash_obj)
  cache_file <- here::here(paste0("data/", cache_name, "_cache.rds"))
  if (file.exists(cache_file)) {
    cc <- readRDS(cache_file)
    if (identical(cc$hash, hash)) return(cc$data)
  }
  out <- fn()
  saveRDS(list(hash = hash, data = out), cache_file)
  out
}

# All plots below are saved as PNG + PDF into reports/Results_files/RQ1|RQ2|RQ3/,
# so every plot lives under exactly one RQ folder -- including the "extreme
# behaviour" plots (Sec. "Extreme behaviour" below), which are split into one
# per RQ's own metric subset for this reason (Report_22/RQ1.Rmd had this as a
# single combined plot across all metrics; split here purely for folder
# consistency, same underlying data/grid).
RESULTS_DIR <- here::here("reports", "Results_files")
for (rq in c("RQ1", "RQ2", "RQ3", "LostVotes")) dir.create(file.path(RESULTS_DIR, rq), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_plot <- function(p, rq, name, width = 13, height = 8) {
  base <- file.path(RESULTS_DIR, rq, name)
  ggsave(paste0(base, ".png"), p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150, bg = "white")
  ggsave(paste0(base, ".pdf"), p, width = width, height = height)
  p
}

# RQ1: delegation behaviour. RQ2: quality of representation (ideological
# drift). RQ3: concentration of voting power. All three are answered off the
# SAME simulation grid (see "Shared design" below) -- one run per (pair,
# fixed-level, seed) cell produces every metric needed for all three RQs at
# once, so the sweep only has to run once.
metrics_rq1 <- c("delegation_rate", "lost_vote_rate", "flickerness", "chain_length")
metrics_rq2 <- c("avg_drift")
metrics_rq3 <- c("top5_power_share", "share_50pct")
metrics_all_rqs <- c(metrics_rq1, metrics_rq2, metrics_rq3)

metric_labels <- c(
  delegation_rate  = "Delegation rate",
  lost_vote_rate   = "Lost-vote rate",
  flickerness      = "Delegation stability",
  chain_length     = "Avg. delegation-chain length",
  avg_drift        = "Avg. ideological drift",
  top5_power_share = "Top-5% voting-power share",
  share_50pct      = "Agents needed for 50% of power"
)
```

## Fixed inputs

```{r rq-fixed-inputs}
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# KEEP IN SYNC WITH REPORT_22 -- these are Report_22's Sec. 6 final
# calibrated values, redefined here rather than sourced from that Rmd
# (more robust to Report_22 changing independently). Update whenever
# Report_22's K/T/r choices change.
#
# N = 1000 (not 500): RQ1.Rmd's previous "paired sweep" used
# n_per_community = 500L, inconsistent with its OWN "extreme behaviour"
# sweep (N=1000) and with Report_22's own small-world corridor requirement
# N > 10*K (Report_22 Sec. 6) -- at K=60 that requires N > 600, which 500
# violates. N=1000 (the value used everywhere else in Report_22/Report_23)
# is used consistently for both sweeps here.
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
CHOSEN_N          <- 1000L
CHOSEN_K          <- 60L
CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS <- 40L   # n_v
CHOSEN_T          <- 80L   # T = n_v * dt = 40 * 2
CHOSEN_C          <- 0.5

lambda_from_forget_rate <- function(forget_pct, h = 5) 1 - (1 - forget_pct / 100)^(1 / h)
LAMBDA_TR         <- lambda_from_forget_rate(50, h = 5)   # 50% of trust signal forgotten over 5 voting rounds

# r_op/r_pw/r_tr needed to reach a given % of each dimension's own
# saturated effect -- Report_22 Sec. 6/4.2, R_SAT_ANCHOR_FINAL read-off.
# Linearly interpolated for any pct in between via pct_to_r_lookup() below.
R_PCT_LOOKUP <- tribble(
  ~pct, ~r_op,     ~r_pw, ~r_tr,
  0,       0.00,     0.00,   0.00,
  10,     13.17,     0.05,   2.09,
  20,     28.85,     0.10,   3.99,
  30,     48.58,     0.15,   6.79,
  40,     72.89,     0.20,   9.76,
  50,    109.53,     0.32,  12.86,
  60,    166.16,     0.51,  15.97,
  70,    243.11,     1.07,  22.97,
  80,    429.31,     3.04,  30.01,
  90,    910.23,     6.59,  48.68,
  100, 16384.00,    64.00, 128.00
)

pct_to_r_lookup <- function(dim_name, pct) {
  col <- switch(dim_name, op = "r_op", pw = "r_pw", tr = "r_tr", stop("unknown dim: ", dim_name))
  approx(R_PCT_LOOKUP$pct, R_PCT_LOOKUP[[col]], xout = pct, rule = 2)$y
}
```

**N = `r CHOSEN_N`, K = `r CHOSEN_K`, T = `r CHOSEN_T`
(`r CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS` voting rounds, Δt = `r CHOSEN_T / CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS`),
c = `r CHOSEN_C`, forget rate = 50% over 5 voting rounds.**

**50 seeds per cell** (raised from an initial 1-seed structural-validation
pass once the plots/folders checked out).

```{r rq-pct-table}
kable(R_PCT_LOOKUP, caption = "r needed to reach a given % of each dimension's own saturated effect (`Report_22` Sec. 6) -- everything below is expressed in these percentages, not raw r")
```

## Extreme behaviour: single-dial vs. isolated dimensions, 0-100%

Before the paired sweep below, a wider look across the full 0-100% range
of each dimension's own saturated effect (`Report_22`'s calibration) --
fixed at N=`r CHOSEN_N`, K=`r CHOSEN_K` -- showing every metric used in
RQ1-3 below, to see where each one saturates rather than assuming the range
used in the paired sweep already captures the full picture. Four
scenarios: **all** ($r_{op},r_{pw},r_{tr}$ all at the same %, each
translated via `R_PCT_LOOKUP`) and each dimension **isolated** in turn (one
dimension at that %, the other two at 0) -- so the joint effect and each
mechanism's own isolated effect are visible side by side. Split into one
plot per RQ below (same grid/data as a single combined plot would use) so
every plot in this report saves into exactly one RQ folder.

```{r rq-extreme-config}
PCT_VALS_EXTREME <- seq(0, 100, by = 10)
N_SEEDS_EXTREME  <- 50L

scenarios_extreme <- tribble(
  ~scenario,     ~use_op, ~use_pw, ~use_tr,
  "all (r=r=r)", TRUE,    TRUE,    TRUE,
  "op only",     TRUE,    FALSE,   FALSE,
  "pw only",     FALSE,   TRUE,    FALSE,
  "trust only",  FALSE,   FALSE,   TRUE
)

```{r rq-extreme-run}
run_extreme_cell <- function(seed, pct, scenario, use_op, use_pw, use_tr) {
  r_op <- if (use_op) pct_to_r_lookup("op", pct) else 0
  r_pw <- if (use_pw) pct_to_r_lookup("pw", pct) else 0
  r_tr <- if (use_tr) pct_to_r_lookup("tr", pct) else 0
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = CHOSEN_N, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K, T = CHOSEN_T,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_TR, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = CHOSEN_C, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  last5 <- max(1L, CHOSEN_T - 4L):CHOSEN_T
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= max(1L, CHOSEN_T - 4L))
  delegation_rate <- mean(res$history_delegation[last5], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, pct = pct, scenario = scenario,
    delegation_rate  = delegation_rate,
    lost_vote_rate   = mean(res$history_lost[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length     = mean(snaps$avg_chain_length_delegators, na.rm = TRUE),
    flickerness      = mean(res$history_flickerness[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_drift        = mean(snaps$avg_drift, na.rm = TRUE),
    top5_power_share = mean(snaps$top5_power_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct      = mean(snaps$share_50pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

grid_extreme <- tidyr::crossing(scenarios_extreme, pct = PCT_VALS_EXTREME, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_EXTREME))

extreme_raw <- run_cached("results_rq_extreme_raw", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_extreme, run_extreme_cell, .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(CHOSEN_N, CHOSEN_K, CHOSEN_T, CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS, CHOSEN_C, N_SEEDS_EXTREME, PCT_VALS_EXTREME,
        scenarios_extreme, LAMBDA_TR, R_PCT_LOOKUP, v = 1))

extreme_summary <- extreme_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_all_rqs), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(scenario, pct, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric   = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels)),
         scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scenarios_extreme$scenario))

plot_extreme <- function(metrics_subset) {
  extreme_summary |>
    filter(metric %in% metric_labels[metrics_subset]) |>
    ggplot(aes(pct, mean_val, colour = scenario, group = scenario)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 1.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = PCT_VALS_EXTREME) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "responsiveness scenario", end = 0.85) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Extreme behaviour -- N=%d, K=%d, all vs. isolated dimensions", CHOSEN_N, CHOSEN_K),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d seed(s) per cell; x = %% of each dimension's own saturated effect (R_PCT_LOOKUP)", N_SEEDS_EXTREME),
         x = "% of own saturated effect", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## Shared design: paired sweep, third dimension held fixed

Same sweep grid for all three RQs. For each pair of responsiveness
dimensions, both are varied *together* in **percentage** terms (same shared
% of each dimension's own saturated effect, translated to that dimension's
own r via `R_PCT_LOOKUP` -- op/pw/tr saturate at wildly different raw r, so
a shared raw value no longer means the same thing across dimensions) across
$\{10,20,...,100\}\%$, while the third dimension is held fixed at one of 3
percentage levels ($0\%, 50\%, 100\%$) -- shown as 3 coloured lines in the
same plot. Repeating this for each of the 3 possible pairs gives 3 plots per
RQ (as many metrics as that RQ needs, faceted), covering all three
responsiveness dimensions:

- $r_{op}, r_{pw}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{tr} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)
- $r_{op}, r_{tr}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{pw} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)
- $r_{pw}, r_{tr}$ varied together $\in \{10,...,100\}\%$, $r_{op} \in \{0,50,100\}\%$ (fixed)

```{r rq-config}
N_SEEDS_PAIR <- 50L

PCT_VALS_PAIR    <- seq(10, 100, by = 10)  # % for the two paired (jointly varied) dimensions
PCT_FIXED_LEVELS <- c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)  # % for the third, held-fixed dimension
```

---

# Simulation grid (answers RQ1, RQ2 and RQ3 at once)

```{r rq-pair-run}
build_pair_grid <- function(pair_label, dim_v1, dim_v2, dim_fixed) {
  df <- tidyr::crossing(pct_v = PCT_VALS_PAIR, pct_f = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS, seed = seq_len(N_SEEDS_PAIR))
  df$pair_label <- pair_label
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_v1)]]    <- pct_to_r_lookup(dim_v1, df$pct_v)
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_v2)]]    <- pct_to_r_lookup(dim_v2, df$pct_v)
  df[[paste0("r_", dim_fixed)]] <- pct_to_r_lookup(dim_fixed, df$pct_f)
  df
}

grid_pair <- bind_rows(
  build_pair_grid("r_op x r_pw (r_tr fixed)", "op", "pw", "tr"),
  build_pair_grid("r_op x r_tr (r_pw fixed)", "op", "tr", "pw"),
  build_pair_grid("r_pw x r_tr (r_op fixed)", "pw", "tr", "op")
)

run_pair_cell <- function(seed, pair_label, pct_v, pct_f, r_op, r_pw, r_tr) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = CHOSEN_N, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K, T = CHOSEN_T,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, gamma = r_tr, lambda = LAMBDA_TR, k1 = 1, k2 = 1,
    self_reliance_c = CHOSEN_C, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )
  last5 <- max(1L, CHOSEN_T - 4L):CHOSEN_T
  snaps <- res$snapshots |> dplyr::filter(round >= max(1L, CHOSEN_T - 4L))
  delegation_rate <- mean(res$history_delegation[last5], na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    seed = seed, pair_label = pair_label, pct_v = pct_v, pct_f = pct_f,
    r_op = r_op, r_pw = r_pw, r_tr = r_tr,
    # RQ1
    delegation_rate  = delegation_rate,
    lost_vote_rate   = mean(res$history_lost[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    chain_length     = mean(snaps$avg_chain_length_delegators, na.rm = TRUE),
    flickerness      = mean(res$history_flickerness[last5], na.rm = TRUE),
    # RQ2
    avg_drift        = mean(snaps$avg_drift, na.rm = TRUE),
    # RQ3
    top5_power_share = mean(snaps$top5_power_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    share_50pct      = mean(snaps$share_50pct, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}

pair_raw <- run_cached("results_rq123_pair_raw", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_pmap_dfr(grid_pair, run_pair_cell, .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(CHOSEN_N, CHOSEN_K, CHOSEN_T, CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS, CHOSEN_C, N_SEEDS_PAIR, PCT_VALS_PAIR, PCT_FIXED_LEVELS, LAMBDA_TR, R_PCT_LOOKUP, v = 1))

pair_summary <- pair_raw |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(metrics_all_rqs), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(pair_label, pct_v, pct_f, metric) |>
  summarise(mean_val = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels)))

# metrics_subset selects which metrics (as their metric_labels) go into this
# particular plot -- each RQ section below passes its own subset, in the
# same order as metrics_rq1/rq2/rq3 above (consistent facet order everywhere).
plot_pair <- function(label, metrics_subset) {
  pair_summary |>
    filter(pair_label == label, metric %in% metric_labels[metrics_subset]) |>
    ggplot(aes(pct_v, mean_val, colour = factor(pct_f, levels = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = PCT_VALS_PAIR) +
    scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "fixed level", end = 0.85, labels = function(x) sprintf("%s%%", x)) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Paired sweep -- %s", label),
         subtitle = sprintf("%d seed(s) per cell; values are %% of each dimension's own saturated effect (R_PCT_LOOKUP), not raw r", N_SEEDS_PAIR),
         x = "shared % of own saturated effect", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## Chain-length distribution across seeds

The paired-sweep plots above show only the mean across `r N_SEEDS_PAIR`
seeds per grid cell -- the violin plots below show the full per-seed
distribution of chain length at each grid point, so spread/skew/outliers the
mean alone hides are visible.

```{r rq1-violin-fn}
plot_violin_chain <- function(label) {
  pair_raw |>
    filter(pair_label == label) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(pct_v, levels = PCT_VALS_PAIR), y = chain_length,
               fill = factor(pct_f, levels = PCT_FIXED_LEVELS))) +
    geom_violin(position = position_dodge(0.8), alpha = 0.8, colour = NA, scale = "width") +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "fixed level", end = 0.85, labels = function(x) sprintf("%s%%", x)) +
    labs(title = sprintf("Chain-length distribution across %d seeds -- %s", N_SEEDS_PAIR, label),
         subtitle = "One violin per grid cell (pct_v x pct_f)",
         x = "shared % of own saturated effect", y = "Avg. delegation-chain length") +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}
```

## Distribution summary -- all RQ1 metrics

Min/max and quartiles alongside the mean, across every individual
(pair, pct_v, pct_f, seed) run in the paired sweep -- not just the
grid-cell averages the plots above show, so the extreme cases seen anywhere
across the whole RQ1 sweep are visible in one place.

```{r rq1-dist-table}
rq1_dist_table <- pair_raw |>
  select(all_of(metrics_rq1)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(metric) |>
  summarise(
    Min    = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1     = quantile(value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean   = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3     = quantile(value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max    = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], levels = unname(metric_labels[metrics_rq1]))) |>
  arrange(metric) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3)))

kable(rq1_dist_table,
      caption = sprintf("RQ1 distribution summary across the full paired sweep (all pct_v x pct_f x pair combinations, %d seeds each)", N_SEEDS_PAIR))
```

# RQ2: quality of political representation

Metric: average ideological drift (`avg_drift`) -- the mean distance between
an agent's own opinion and the opinion of the agent who ultimately casts a
vote on its behalf.

Expected: $r_{op}$ reduces drift (dissimilar neighbours become less
attractive delegates); $r_{pw}$ increases drift (powerful delegates stay
attractive even when ideologically distant); $r_{tr}$ reduces drift, same
mechanism as $r_{op}$. Because attractiveness is multiplicative, the joint
$r_{op} \times r_{pw}$ effect is expected to favour the opinion term (net
drift reduction), not a simple additive combination of the two individual
effects.

# RQ3: concentration of voting power

Metrics: voting-power share held by the top 5% of agents (`top5_power_share`)
and the fraction of agents needed to collectively hold 50% of total voting
power (`share_50pct`).

Expected: $r_{op}$ lowers concentration (more agents vote directly);
$r_{pw}$ raises concentration (rich-get-richer -- already-powerful agents
become more attractive delegates). For the joint $r_{op} \times r_{pw}$
effect: as in RQ2, low opinion-based attractiveness is expected to constrain
how much high voting power can raise a neighbour's overall attractiveness --
so increasing both together should yield *lower* concentration than high
$r_{pw}$ alone.

```{r rq3-extreme-plot, fig.height=8}
p <- plot_extreme(metrics_rq3)
save_plot(p, "RQ3", "extreme", height = 8)
p
```

# Lost votes: cycle mechanics

A closer look at *how* votes actually get lost -- not just the lost-vote
*rate* (RQ1 above), but the underlying cycle mechanism: how many agents are
caught in a cycle at any given moment, what size those cycles are, and how
quickly an individual agent escapes one once caught. Uses
`Network.R`'s `lost_agent_ids` (per-round, which specific agent ids have a
lost/NA vote -- added for this section; `cycle_breakdown`, used elsewhere,
only has per-round *counts* by cycle length, not agent identity, so it can't
answer "is agent i still lost next round").

Run at the fully calibrated model (r_op=r_pw=r_tr=100% of each one's own
saturated effect, r_ig=0 -- no group dimension here), N/K/T as in "Fixed
inputs" above, over a steady-state window (last 30 of `r CHOSEN_T` rounds),
20 seeds.

```{r lost-votes-config}
N_SEEDS_LOST <- 20L
LOST_WINDOW  <- (CHOSEN_T - 29):CHOSEN_T        # last 30 rounds, steady state
```

```{r lost-votes-fn}
run_lost_votes_cell <- function(seed) {
  res <- simulate_liquid_democracy(
    seed = seed, n_per_community = CHOSEN_N, n_communities = 1, node_degree = CHOSEN_K, T = CHOSEN_T,
    n_voting_rounds = CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS,
    r_op = pct_to_r_lookup("op", 100), r_pw = pct_to_r_lookup("pw", 100), gamma = pct_to_r_lookup("tr", 100),
    lambda = LAMBDA_TR, k1 = 1, k2 = 1, self_reliance_c = CHOSEN_C, trust_mode = "relaxation",
    sigma_opinion = "auto", fast_path = TRUE, p_rewire = 0.05
  )

  # A. Cycle-size distribution: raw (round, cycle_length, n_agents) rows,
  # tagged with seed -- aggregated across ALL seeds afterwards by summing
  # n_agents per cycle_length and dividing by a FIXED denominator
  # (N_SEEDS_LOST * length(LOST_WINDOW)), rather than averaging per seed
  # here. That avoids relying on every seed having at least one cycle: a
  # seed/round with zero cycles anywhere just contributes no rows at all
  # (cycle_breakdown can even be completely empty, 0 rows/0 columns, for a
  # seed where no cycle ever formed in the whole run -- e.g. plausible at
  # the fully-saturated r=100% used here) -- the fixed denominator still
  # accounts for it correctly instead of silently excluding it from the mean.
  size_dist <- if (nrow(res$cycle_breakdown) > 0) {
    res$cycle_breakdown |>
      dplyr::filter(round %in% LOST_WINDOW) |>
      dplyr::mutate(seed = seed)
  } else {
    tibble(round = integer(0), cycle_length = integer(0), n_agents = integer(0), seed = integer(0))
  }

  n_lost_per_round <- tibble(
    seed = seed, round = LOST_WINDOW,
    n_lost = lengths(res$lost_agent_ids[LOST_WINDOW])
  )

  # B. One-step recovery: for every consecutive round pair (t, t+1) in the
  # window, of the agents lost AT t, what fraction are NOT lost at t+1 --
  # i.e. "was this round's lost vote no longer lost next round". Computed
  # for every t in the window (not just a handful of reference points) for
  # a more robust estimate; this is a per-cohort rate, not a per-agent
  # trajectory -- no tracking of any individual agent beyond one round.
  recovery <- purrr::map_dfr(LOST_WINDOW[-length(LOST_WINDOW)], function(t) {
    base   <- res$lost_agent_ids[[t]]
    n_base <- length(base)
    if (n_base == 0) return(tibble(seed = seed, round = t, n_base = 0L, frac_recovered = NA_real_))
    tibble(seed = seed, round = t, n_base = n_base,
           frac_recovered = mean(!(base %in% res$lost_agent_ids[[t + 1]])))
  })

  list(size_dist = size_dist, n_lost_per_round = n_lost_per_round, recovery = recovery)
}

lost_votes_raw <- run_cached("results_lost_votes_raw", function() {
  plan(multisession, workers = N_WORKERS)
  out <- future_map(seq_len(N_SEEDS_LOST), run_lost_votes_cell, .options = furrr_options(seed = NULL))
  plan(sequential)
  out
}, list(CHOSEN_N, CHOSEN_K, CHOSEN_T, CHOSEN_VOTING_RDS, CHOSEN_C, N_SEEDS_LOST, LOST_WINDOW,
        LAMBDA_TR, R_PCT_LOOKUP, v = 3))
# v = 3: Network.R's cycle_breakdown now actually carries a `round` column
# (dplyr::count() was silently dropping it, see Network.R fix) -- this is
# what the earlier run errored on ("match needs vectors" from filtering on
# a nonexistent `round` column).

size_dist_all        <- purrr::map_dfr(lost_votes_raw, "size_dist")
n_lost_per_round_all  <- purrr::map_dfr(lost_votes_raw, "n_lost_per_round")
recovery_all          <- purrr::map_dfr(lost_votes_raw, "recovery")
```

## How many agents are stuck in a cycle, and how big are the cycles?

```{r lost-votes-size-table}
n_seed_rounds <- N_SEEDS_LOST * length(LOST_WINDOW)   # fixed denominator, see run_lost_votes_cell() comment

size_dist_summary <- size_dist_all |>
  group_by(cycle_length) |>
  summarise(total_agents = sum(n_agents), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(cycle_length) |>
  mutate(mean_n_agents   = total_agents / n_seed_rounds,
         mean_pct_of_pop = round(mean_n_agents / CHOSEN_N * 100, 2),
         mean_n_agents   = round(mean_n_agents, 2)) |>
  select(cycle_length, mean_n_agents, mean_pct_of_pop)

kable(size_dist_summary,
      caption = sprintf("Average number of agents (out of N=%d) stuck in a cycle of each size, at a random steady-state round (last 30 of %d rounds, %d seeds)",
                         CHOSEN_N, CHOSEN_T, N_SEEDS_LOST))
cat(sprintf("\n**Total: on average %.1f agents (%.2f%% of the population) are lost to a cycle of some size at any given steady-state round.**\n",
            sum(size_dist_summary$mean_n_agents), sum(size_dist_summary$mean_pct_of_pop)))
```

```{r lost-votes-timeseries-plot, fig.height=5}
p <- n_lost_per_round_all |>
  group_by(round) |>
  summarise(mean_n_lost = mean(n_lost), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(round, mean_n_lost)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") + geom_point(size = 1.8, colour = "black") +
  labs(title = "Agents lost to a cycle per round (steady-state window)",
       subtitle = sprintf("Mean across %d seeds, r_op=r_pw=r_tr=100%%", N_SEEDS_LOST),
       x = "Round", y = "N agents lost") +
  ylim(0, NA)
save_plot(p, "LostVotes", "n_lost_per_round", height = 5)
p
```

## Round-to-round recovery: was a lost vote still lost next round?

For every pair of consecutive rounds in the steady-state window: of the
agents whose vote was lost at round $t$, what share are *not* lost at round
$t+1$ (i.e. recovered)?

```{r lost-votes-recovery-plot, fig.height=5}
recovery_by_round <- recovery_all |>
  filter(n_base > 0) |>
  group_by(round) |>
  summarise(mean_frac_recovered = mean(frac_recovered), n_obs = n(), .groups = "drop")

p <- recovery_by_round |>
  ggplot(aes(round, mean_frac_recovered)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") + geom_point(size = 1.8, colour = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Share of a round's lost votes that are not lost the following round",
       subtitle = sprintf("Mean across %d seeds, r_op=r_pw=r_tr=100%%", N_SEEDS_LOST),
       x = "Round t", y = "% recovered by round t+1") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
save_plot(p, "LostVotes", "recovery_by_round", height = 5)
p
```

```{r lost-votes-recovery-note, results = "asis"}
recovery_overall <- recovery_all |> filter(n_base > 0) |> summarise(x = mean(frac_recovered)) |> pull(x)
cat(sprintf(
  "**On average, %.1f%% of agents whose vote is lost to a cycle in a given round are no longer lost the very next round**, averaged across the steady-state window (last %d rounds) and %d seeds.\n",
  recovery_overall * 100, length(LOST_WINDOW), N_SEEDS_LOST
))
```
